calls.reason: The forecast depends on OpenAI failing. Oracle's 27 Oct 2026 announcement of a new partnership shows OpenAI still operating, so there are no consequences to compare yet.

OpenAI closed a $122B round, so it is still drawing in capital. But the private-credit part rests only on early Broadcom talks naming Apollo and Blackstone, with no deal done, and nothing shows other firms were starved of funds.

Newer chips are clearly faster (Blackwell benchmarks), but the resale index shows rebounds and H100 servers holding price, and no cohort has been followed through a full life. The evidence is mixed and the claim has no deadline.

NVIDIA's $2B CoreWeave stake and CoreWeave's contract-backed $2.6B loan are separate facts. Nothing links them into the claimed NVIDIA-money-to-debt-to-GPU-purchase chain, or shows the motive or the profit premise.

Hugging Face's guide says sampling is not deterministic, and Thinking Machines got 80 different completions at temperature 0 under default settings. Identical outputs needed custom kernels, which weakens only the 'because probabilistic' part.

CoreWeave's 10-K gives Microsoft 67% and caps every other customer below 10%. Nebius reports only annualised run-rate figures. Neither breaks out customers well enough to rebuild the roughly $1B remainder across all three companies.
